subject: BrightPath: model fit, safety eval plan & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha@brightpath.health>
Cc: Dr. Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@brightpath.health>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: BrightPath discovery — model fit notes + proposed evals

Hi Samantha (and Aaron),

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap from our discovery and the concrete next steps I promised: 

What I heard (short):
- Primary use case: triage assistant that summarizes intake form + flags high-risk phrasing for clinician review.
- Data: historically documented intake forms + anonymized chat transcripts (~120k turns). No PHI in files you can share; you will confirm export path.
- Success criteria: >92% recall on high-risk flags in our internal benchmark; average summary ROUGE-L > 0.6 for 2-turn summaries. Latency target: 300–500ms p50.

Suggested model candidates for initial eval (based on latency & safety needs):
- rdx-1.3f-quant (fast, low token cost, good refusal behavior in internal tests)
- rdx-2.7f-safety-tuned (stronger safety/guardrail defaults; slightly higher cost)
- open-gpt-med-1 (baseline open model from your team for comparison)

Proposed eval plan / timeline:
1) You share a redacted sample export (5–10k records) and your risk classification taxonomy — by Tue 4/20.
2) We run a 2-week automated eval: benchmarks (recall/precision for flags), summary quality (ROUGE/semantic sim), and refusal/safety tests (sensitive-domain prompts).
3) Deliverables: evaluation report + recommended model profile and a prompt-set to guard against risky completions — by Fri 5/06.

Safety & refusal focus (what we'll test):
- Sensitive domain detection: drugs, self-harm, child-safety phrasing.
- Refusal clarity: ensure model either returns a safe refusal or routes to human with minimal hallucination.
- Prompt injection resilience and role-assistant adherence.

Next actions (mutual):
- Samantha: share redacted sample + security contact for RFI (procurement is CC'd) — target 4/20.
- Ben: spin up baseline runs (rdx-1.3f-quant + rdx-2.7f-safety-tuned) and share initial benchmark link by 4/22.
- Marissa: technical deep-dive on prompt sets + guardrail suggestions (I'll loop her on follow-up).

Attachments: I attached an initial prompt set and the RFI template we typically use.

Thanks — looking forward to the samples.

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Samantha Li <samantha@brightpath.health>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightpath.health>, Dr. Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@brightpath.health>
Date: 2027-04-18T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightPath discovery — model fit notes + proposed evals

Thanks Ben — the recap is perfect and captures the call. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Data export: we can provide 7,500 de-identified intake records (PHI redacted) by 4/20. IT will deliver a CSV + jsonl schema.
2) Security contact: procurement will own the RFI intake; attaching procurement email for direct follow-up (they're CC'd). They may ask for SOC 2 evidence and encryption-at-rest details.
3) Safety concerns: our compliance lead is particularly worried about the model under-reporting suicidal ideation when phrased indirectly. Can you include focused refusal/responsiveness tests for oblique phrasing?

One scheduling ask: would it be possible to have a short 30-min tech session with your SE to walk Aaron and our engineering lead through the prompt flow? Aaron is available 4/21 or 4/22 afternoon PST.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Samantha
Samantha Li
Head of Product, BrightPath Health
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightPath discovery — model fit notes + proposed evals

Marissa / Neha — forwarding the prospect thread. Key asks:
- Focused safety/oblique-suicidal phrasing tests (Samantha called this out). We should construct a 50-case prompt set that includes indirect phrasing, cultural idioms, and misspellings.
- Please include a suggested guardrail template: refusal templates + escalation routing (e.g., flag + verbatim excerpt + confidence score).
- Can you confirm the best model quantization/profile to hit ~400ms p50 for single-turn summarization on our dedicated n1-gpu pool? If rdx-1.3f-quant won't reliably meet it with KV caching off, call it out.

I attached the initial prompt set and the RFI they sent. I'll schedule the 30-min tech session once you confirm availability 4/21 or 4/22.

Thanks — Ben

Attachment stubs: initial_prompt_set_v1.txt, BrightPath_RFI_Security_Questions.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Li <samantha@brightpath.health>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightPath discovery — model fit notes + proposed evals

Ben / Neha / Samantha — thanks for the context. Quick plan from SE side: 

1) Prompt & safety test plan (deliver by 4/22):
- Build 50-case oblique-suicide prompt set: 20 oblique phrasing, 10 idioms/cultural variants, 10 misspellings/typos, 10 complex contexts that combine medication requests + self-harm mentions.
- Include expected model responses and a binary pass/fail rubric for refusal clarity and safe routing.

2) Model performance check (deliver by 4/22):
- Run microbenchmarks on rdx-1.3f-quant + rdx-2.7f-safety-tuned using a 1k sample subset with target payloads; report p50/p95 and token cost estimates.
- If rdx-1.3f-quant p50 >450ms, recommend rdx-2.7f-safety-tuned or a tuned-slim variant for the latency budget.

3) Tech session: 30 minutes on 4/22 at 2:00pm PST works for me; Ben please confirm and I'll send a calendar invite (I'll cover prompt flow, guardrail hooks, and integration notes for logs/alerts).

4) Compliance asks: we'll attach SOC 2 summary + KMS encryption doc to the RFI response. Neha — can you own security evidence and draft answers for the RFI?

Samantha — we'll keep the testing conservative: the first run will intentionally bias toward safe refusals (we can tune for recall later). Expect an interim report by 4/22 and a full evaluation report by 5/06 as Ben outlined.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
